v1.howToRead: HOW TO READ IT: choose the single instant that best shows what happens in the moment and paint that, as if the viewer stands inside the scene. When someone speaks, look at what the words do. If they tell of something in another place or time (history, a memory, a story or parable, a dream, vision or prophecy), paint what they tell, in its own time and place and its own era's dress, and leave the teller and listeners out unless the text puts them inside it. If they address the people present, or the moment shows the act of speaking, paint the speaker and listeners where they are. Never both in one picture: no inset, bubble or second scene beside the speaker. Figures of speech and comparisons are not literal objects. Infer time, light, weather and any place not given under SETTING from the text and context.
v1.rule3: Nothing from outside the era of what is painted.
